chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

We said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Is the turban part of the shroud for the deceased?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, the obligatory shroud is three garments and a complete garment, not less than that, which covers his entire body. So whatever increases beyond that is Sunnah, up to reaching five garments. So whatever increases beyond that is an innovation (bid'ah). And the turban is Sunnah.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ordered with the turban, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was turbaned.'

And the Sheikh, Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), sent to us a dinar when Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hazza' died, while we were in Medina, and ordered us to buy him embalming material (hanut) and a turban, so we did it.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum number of garments required for a valid Islamic shroud, and is the turban obligatory?
ai.summary: This hadith delineates the fiqh of the kafan, establishing the obligatory minimum as three garments plus one complete covering, while categorizing the turban as a recommended Sunnah rather than a fard component. It highlights the continuity of this practice through the Prophet’s example and the specific instruction of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to purchase a turban for Abu Ubaydah al-Haddad, illustrating the Imams' emphasis on dignified burial attire beyond the strict legal minimum.
